text.p: ROME, May 13 (Reuter - Britain's General Electric Co Plc and Finmeccanica of Italy said on Tuesday a joint study on linking up in the defence industry was making good progress.

A statement issued by the two companies in Rome said the study, looking at possible collaborative ventures between their respective subsidiaries, GEC-Marconi and Alenia Difesa, "is proceeding regularly with satisfactory results."
Milan business newspaper Il Sole-24 Ore reported on Tuesday that GEC's interest in acquiring part of France's state-controlled Thomson-CSF had cast a shadow over an agreement with Alenia.
"It is evident that GEC will do everything to conquer...Thomson. If it succeeds, Alenia could be cut out (of the deal)," said Il Sole.
French electronics group Alcatel Alsthom and bidding partner Dassault are currently battling Lagardere to take control of Thomson. Alcatel has said it would talk to GEC and others if it won.
The statement said GEC and Finmeccanica were in close contact "at the highest levels of the two companies in the full spirit of the agreements made."
GEC and Finmeccanica signed a memorandum of understanding to explore opportunities for defence collaboration in March.

Fabiano Fabiani, stood down as chairman of Finmeccanica last month after its parent company, stateholding IRI, ordered him to reverse his industrial strategy of bringing the group's interests under a single umbrella.
